content: If you are patient in one moment of anger, you will escape a hundred days of sorrow.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Ren de yi shi zhi qi, mian de bai ri zhi you (忍得一时之气)
explanation: Anger is an intoxicating flash of poison that lasts only a few minutes, but the reckless words barked or bridges burned during those sixty seconds can take months or decades of agony to rebuild. Cultivating the pause between provocation and reaction is true mastery.
practicalInsight: When someone offends you today, do not speak for sixty seconds. Breathe deeply until the fiery impulse clears.
reflectionPrompt: Recall a time when unbridled anger cost you dearly. What would your life look like if you mastered that sixty-second pause?
